The Wine Corner

Savoie: France’s Alpine wines

By Pierre DuMont · October 7, 2026 · 3 min read

High in the French Alps, where vineyards cling to steep slopes beneath snow-capped peaks, the wines of Savoie are gaining attention for their distinctive character and sense of place.

For generations, Savoie’s vineyards have been closely tied to the region’s mountain communities. Today, a new generation of winemakers is bringing renewed energy to an area once known primarily to French locals and Alpine holidaymakers. The result is a collection of wines that can be remarkably fresh, mineral-driven and unlike those produced in France’s better-known regions.

White wines dominate Savoie’s production, with the Jacquère grape playing a central role. Light-bodied and crisp, Jacquère produces wines with lively acidity and subtle floral and citrus notes, making them natural companions to local mountain cuisine. Altesse, another important white grape, produces the more structured and aromatic wines known as Roussette de Savoie. My favorite wine is Chignin-Bergeron, which is made from the Rhone Valley’s Roussanne grape.

The region also has its own red specialties. Mondeuse, a traditional local grape, creates deeply colored wines with bright acidity, peppery spice and dark-fruit flavors. Gamay and Pinot Noir are also planted, adding further variety to the region’s offerings.

Savoie’s geography is central to its identity. Vineyards are scattered across valleys and foothills, often at considerable elevations. The cool Alpine climate allows grapes to ripen slowly while retaining the acidity that gives the wines their characteristic freshness.

That freshness is particularly well suited to Savoie’s traditional foods: fondue, raclette, tartiflette and other rich mountain dishes. The wines cut through the richness of the cheese and potatoes, creating a pairing that reflects the region itself.

As interest in distinctive, terroir-driven wines continues to grow, Savoie is increasingly finding a place on the international wine map. Its bottles offer something increasingly sought after by modern wine drinkers: wines with a strong sense of origin, tradition and landscape.

Philippe Viallet: a family name in Savoie wine

At the foot of Mont Granier in France’s Alpine Savoie region, the name Philippe Viallet has become closely associated with the area’s distinctive wines. The family wine story began in 1966, when Marcel and Yvonne Viallet acquired a small vineyard in Apremont. Their sons, Pierre and Philippe, later continued the family business, with Philippe helping to develop it into both a wine producer and wine merchant.

The Viallet range reflects the diversity of Savoie’s mountain vineyards. Among its bestknown wines is Apremont, made from the Jacquère grape. It is a light, crisp and refreshing white wine with bright acidity. Another important wine is Chignin-Bergeron, made from the Roussanne grape and generally fuller and more aromatic, with flavors of ripe fruit and flowers.

Roussette de Savoie, made from the Altesse grape, offers another distinctive style, while the winery’s red wines include Mondeuse, one of Savoie’s traditional varieties, as well as Pinot Noir and Gamay.

The winery also produces Crémant de Savoie, a sparkling wine, along with rosé wines.

Philippe Viallet’s wines offer a taste of the Alpine landscape. Fresh, lively and closely connected to local grape varieties, they demonstrate why Savoie is attracting growing interest from wine drinkers looking for wines with a strong sense of place and a character of their own.

NV Viallet Crémant de Savoie

A sparkling wine made in the style of Champagne, this is light and refreshing, dry and crisp with tiny bubbles. At $13 a bottle it is an incredible bargain.

2024 G.G. Bouvet Roussette de Savoie

This is another of the Viallet labels and Roussette is their name for the Altesse grape. It is a charming white wine, clean and crisp with floral notes of honeysuckle and orange blossoms. On the palate it shows peach and apricot flavors. Perfect aperitif.

2024 Vialet Chignin-Bergeron

Chignin-Bergeron is the name in Savoie for the Roussanne grape from the Rhone Valley. It is my favorite of the Savoie wines. Richer and fuller and round in the mouth with good weight and structure. Flavors of melons and pears and a long lingering finish. Excellent effort.

2023 Clos de la Galeze Mondeuse

Mondeuse is related to the Syrah grape and makes the best red wines in the Savoie. It is medium-bodied with flavors of cherries and currants and moderate tannins. It has ample acid and should drink well for five years.
